extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involves customized workflows for each evaluation dimension, generally following three stages: preprocessing, annotation (using VLMs, detection models, or human experts), and Q&A format generation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of large-scale real-world robotic datasets combined with curated in-house collections, featuring diverse task settings such as single-arm, dual-arm, and mobile manipulation, as well as multi-view scenes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were created using a hybrid approach: Gemini generated initial structured annotations (task summaries, instructions, metadata) which were then refined by human annotators. Execution-level failures were labeled by experts. For quality control, 20 professionally trained annotators conducted inspections to validate linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness, utilizing a majority-vote strategy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was validated for linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy was applied, and items that all models failed to solve were subjected to manual review and correction.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini and other LLMs were used to generate initial structured annotations, segment video steps for temporal grounding, and rewrite explicit instructions into implicit ones.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data manipulation included sampling representative frames for affordance annotation and synthesizing planning-level failures by perturbing correct instructions to augment the dataset where real-world failure data was lacking.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing involved standardizing data into multiple-choice QA formats and a two-stage quality control process. This included applying general filters for image quality and task validity, task-specific filters (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks), and a post-construction filtering step where items solved correctly by all models were removed.

name.evidence: we introduce RoboBench, a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains.

description.evidence: we introduce RoboBench, a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains.
